hidden_target.material_initial_state: As-deposited, approximately 1 μm-thick FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy-alloy multilayer coatings produced from Al0.2CrFeNi and Al targets.
hidden_target.intervention: The modulation period (individual layer thickness, λ) was varied among 8, 16, 32, and 80 nm by RF magnetron sputtering to create multilayers dominated respectively by coherent heterointerfaces (M8), semicoherent heterointerfaces (M16), or grain boundaries (M32 and M80), followed by nanoindentation creep testing.
hidden_target.conditions: Deposition used a base pressure of about 5 × 10^-4 Pa, Ar flow of 100 sccm, working pressure of 0.3 Pa, 150 W on the HEA target, alternating 0/30 W on the Al target, and a 1 h deposition. Room-temperature nanoindentation used a 5 mN maximum load, loading rates of 1, 0.1, and 0.01 mN/s, a 100 s hold, and 20 s unloading; indentation depths were maintained at approximately 1/10–1/7 of the coating thickness.
hidden_target.structural_mediator: The key mediator was interface coherency. M16 contained semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces with misfit dislocations; M8 had coherent interfaces with continuous atomic planes; and M32/M80 were dominated by grain boundaries because λ exceeded the approximately 20 nm grain diameter. Stress-induced interfacial amorphization in M16 is invoked based partly on the authors' prior MD/HRTEM work rather than directly established here.
hidden_target.mechanism: Semicoherent interfaces strongly block dislocation glide, causing dislocation pileup and localized high stress. The authors propose that this promotes interfacial amorphization, whose free volume, disorder, and high-energy crystal–amorphous boundaries lower atomic-migration barriers and enable rate-limited atomic diffusion or interface slip while redistributing stress. Coherent interfaces transmit dislocations more readily, and coherent-interface- or grain-boundary-dominated samples therefore deform mainly by dislocation slip or climb.
hidden_target.predicted_outcome: Relative to multilayers dominated by coherent interfaces or grain boundaries, the λ = 16 nm semicoherent multilayer exhibits the greatest room-temperature creep resistance and a transition from dislocation-mediated creep to atomic-diffusion- or interface-slip-mediated creep.
hidden_target.baseline: The comparison baseline comprises M8 (λ = 8 nm, coherent interfaces) and M32/M80 (λ = 32/80 nm, grain-boundary-dominated interfaces), which show predominantly dislocation-mediated creep.
hidden_target.boundary: The result applies to the studied approximately 1 μm FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni sputtered multilayers under room-temperature, 5 mN nanoindentation creep at loading rates of 1–0.01 mN/s. Absolute creep displacement and steady-state-rate trends changed with loading rate, but the authors report the λ = 16 nm sample as having the strongest creep resistance based particularly on the stress-exponent trend. No elevated-temperature or macroscopic-creep boundary was established.
hidden_target.discriminating_measurement: XRD and TEM/IFFT distinguished phase peaks and coherent versus semicoherent interfaces. Load–displacement and normalized displacement–dwell-time nanoindentation curves measured creep displacement and strain rate, while linear fits of ln(strain rate) versus ln(flow stress) yielded the creep stress exponent n used to distinguish diffusion/interface-slip creep (n around 1–2, with nanoindentation values potentially somewhat higher) from dislocation creep (n > 3).
hidden_target.actual_result: M16 had the highest reported creep resistance and the minimum stress exponent: n = 2.6 at 1 mN/s, 1.5 at 0.1 mN/s, and 2.3 at 0.01 mN/s, consistent with atomic diffusion or interface slip. M8, M32, and M80 generally had n > 3 and were assigned dislocation-slip/climb creep. At 1 mN/s, creep displacement fell from about 24 nm for M80 to 10 nm for M16, then rose to 19 nm for M8; steady-state creep rate similarly fell from 5.7 × 10^-4 s^-1 at λ = 80 nm to 3.1 × 10^-4 s^-1 at 16 nm, then rose to 4.1 × 10^-4 s^-1 at 8 nm. Loading-rate reduction altered displacement and rate trends and produced pop-ins at 0.01 mN/s, but the stress-exponent trend retained a minimum at M16.
